title: Election 2026 live updates: Democrats unseat Sen. Susan Collins in Maine
text:
Election results 2026 live updates: Democrats win Congress, defeat Susan Collins 
 LIVE COVERAGE Updated now Election 2026 live updates: Democrats unseat Sen. Susan Collins in Maine
 Democrat Troy Jackson has won the Maine Senate race, NBC News projects. It’s been a strong night for his party; Democrats will have full control of Congress beginning in January.
 Save Add NBC News to Google Updated November 04, 2026, 1:33 AM EST By NBC News What to know on Election Day 
 DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF CONGRESS: Democrats will take control of the House and the Senate in January, NBC News projects. The party has flipped seven Senate seats so far, in Iowa , Kansas , Ohio , Maine , North Carolina , South Carolina and Texas .
 HOUSE MARGIN: An NBC News analysis shows that Democrats will win at least 252 House seats — an estimate that could still tick up or down by a few seats but will be well beyond the 218 needed to secure a majority.
 GOVERNOR RACES: Democrats have also flipped governorships in Texas , Georgia , Ohio and Iowa .
 NBC NEWS EXIT POLLS: NBC News Exit Polls showed a dissatisfied electorate, with President Donald Trump’s disapproval rating at a dismal 62% and more than three-quarters of voters saying they disapprove of the job Congress is doing, as well. Nearly half of voters said they view the election as an opportunity to rebuke Trump.
 WHERE TO WATCH: Follow along this evening for results, detailed election data , analysis and on-the-ground reporting from correspondents across the country. Steve Kornack is live at the big board and NBC News primetime coverage will be going all night.

 Benson, who serves as Michigan’s secretary of state, defeated Republican Rep. John James, who now finds himself without an elected office. It’s the first time since the 1960s that a Democrat will succeed a Democratic governor.

 25m ago / 1:08 AM EST Mike Rogers tells supporters 'there is a path for us to win this thing' 
 Michigan GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers took the stage just before 1 a.m. ET to tell his supporters to go home but not to lose hope.
 "We're going to ask you all to go home," Rogers said. "It's going to be a long night, but let me tell you this: There is a path for us to win this thing right here." 
 Spencer Platt / Getty 
 NBC News has projected that the Michigan Senate race is leaning toward Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed. 
 Rogers acknowledged the sweep of Democratic victories tonight but declared to his supporters that "it's coming our way." 
 "We're very, very confident in the votes that are out, and we're going to turn this thing around," Rogers said. "So don't listen to all the nonsense you see up there. We're going to get this done."
 27m ago / 1:05 AM EST Obama says new Democratic majorities must 'lay the groundwork for the future' 
 Former President Barack Obama celebrated the blue wave that swept Democratic candidates into office nationwide, writing on social media that "the American people sent a clear message — they want a politics that brings people together rather than divides them, and leaders who offer concrete solutions to the challenges they face."
 Spencer Platt / Getty 
 "These results were only possible because outstanding candidates stepped forward in every region of the country — including in areas once considered long shots," Obama said. "They came from different backgrounds and represented a range of political perspectives, but were united by shared values, a belief in public service, and a commitment to putting the people of their districts and states first."
 Obama outlined his vision for the incoming Democratic majorities in the Senate and the House, writing in part: "While this administration has another two years in office, our job now is to roll up our sleeves, make changes wherever we have the power to do so, prevent further damage, and lay the groundwork for the future."
 Obama, who left the White House nearly 10 years ago, campaigned alongside a range of high-profile Democratic candidates in the final weeks of the race, including Senate candidates Jon Ossoff of Georgia and Sherrod Brown of Ohio.

 35m ago / 12:58 AM EST Rep. Mike Lawler concedes to Democrat Cait Conley in New York battleground 
 Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., took the stage at his watch party in Rockland County to tell his supporters he had conceded the race to Democrat Cait Conley. 
 NBC News has not yet projected a winner in the race for New York's 17th Congressional District, a key battleground. 
 “About 20 minutes ago, I called my opponent, Cait Conley, and offered my congratulations to her,” Lawler said just before 11 p.m. ET. "When all of the votes are counted tomorrow in Westchester, it's going to be pretty clear that we will be short."
 Kena Betancur / Getty 
 The announcement came after Westchester officials said earlier in the day that some ballots would not be counted until tomorrow due to some ballot tabulators malfunctioning. Ballots from those tabulators will be counted tomorrow starting at 11 a.m. ET. 
 "It's something that I have never been afforded in any of my elections, a concession on election night, and I fundamentally believe it's the right thing to do," Lawler said. "And so I congratulate Cait on her win and wish her well as our next member of Congress." 
 Lawler, who crossed the aisle to vote with Democrats on certain issues as a GOP congressman, thanked several Republican leaders, including Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Notably, Lawler did not name Trump.

 52m ago / 12:41 AM EST NBC News Exit Poll in Minnesota: Peggy Flanagan wins Senate seat with backing from young and urban voters 
 Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s lieutenant governor, is projected to win the state's Senate race with solid support from 96% of Democrats, as well as significant backing from urban voters, voters under age 30, college graduates, first-time midterm voters, women and moderates, the NBC News Exit Poll found.
 Among the 63% of voters who said they believe fraud in Minnesota government agencies and programs is a “major problem,” 69% voted for Flanagan's opponent, Republican candidate Michele Tafoya. Among the 31% of voters who rated the fraud scandal a “minor problem,” nearly all, 94%, voted for Flanagan.
 53m ago / 12:40 AM EST Senate Republican leader says caucus will work with Trump to stop Democrats' agenda 
 Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., posted on X about the election results tonight, listing GOP achievements over the past two years and striking a defiant tone toward Democrats.
 “As we head into 2027, Senate Republicans will not stand idly by as the far-left, socialist wing of the Democrat Party attempts to unwind everything we’ve done,” Thune wrote . “Thankfully, we still have President Trump in the White House, and we’ll work with him to stop the worst impulses of Democrat extremism. We cannot let their fringe positions become the mainstream.”

 GOP Sen. Susan Collins, who was locked in a competitive re-election race against Democrat Troy Jackson in Maine, said in a statement that she'd conceded the race.
 Sen. Susan Collins Concedes in Maine Senate race 02:53 
 “It has been the honor of my life to serve the people of Maine in the United States Senate. I'm proud of all I have been able to accomplish for our state and for our country in the past 30 years," Collins said. "I called Troy Jackson tonight to congratulate him and to assure him that my staff and I will work to ensure a smooth transition.”
 NBC News has not yet projected the outcome of the race, characterizing it as too early to call.

 2h ago / 12:30 AM EST NBC News Exit Poll: Michigan voters split on El-Sayed’s views 
 A major question looming over the Michigan Senate race was whether Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s policy positions would win support from voters in a state that voted twice for Trump. 
 After El-Sayed drew attention for championing “Medicare for All” and for his criticism of U.S. aid to Israel, the state's voters are roughly split over whether his views are too extreme, according to the NBC News Exit Poll . 
 Voters provided a starker assessment of the Republican candidate, former Rep. Mike Rogers. Michigan voters said Rogers is too supportive of Trump by a 24-point margin. 
 2h ago / 12:28 AM EST Mike Rogers is falling far behind Trump's 2024 numbers in key rural areas 
 GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers is lagging behind the margins Trump won by in key rural Michigan counties in 2024 — areas he'll need to take the seat. 
 These counties are very small, but collectively, they are do add up. Trump won by big margins in these smaller rural counties in 2024. So far, Rogers has not gotten the same level of support in any of the dozen or so counties here. 
 If there is going to be a path for Rogers tonight in Michigan, he needs an underperformance from Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Oakland County, the home county of Rep. Haley Stevens, who backed Rogers, and where there is a large Jewish population. 
 Show more With 83% of the vote counted in Oakland, El-Sayed is holding a lead. Rogers needs that lead to be cut to the single digits, which it is not at as of now, but El-Sayed is performing worse in Oakland than expected. 
 Democrats are overperforming tonight in the counties that they won in 2024 by large margins. In Oakland, we're actually really seeing very little movement in the Democrats' direction relative to 2024. 
 That speaks, I think, to some of the concerns Democrats had and some of the hopes Republicans have had about El-Sayed's candidacy's giving pause to traditionally Democratic voters, especially in the suburbs and among Jewish voters. 
 2h ago / 12:26 AM EST Trump's final two years comes down to one word: 'Veto' 
 In not so many words, Trump conceded that his powers will be limited as the lame duck executive leader of a divided federal government for the next two years.
 Trump posted a photo of a red baseball cap with the word "VETO" in similar fashion to his Make America Great Again cap .
 While Democrats will soon control both sides of Capitol Hill, they'll fall short of a two-thirds majority that would be needed to override presidential vetoes.
 2h ago / 12:24 AM EST Trump softens tone toward Democrats 
 We’re getting a little bit of whiplash here from Trump, who has been lashing out at Republicans and offering a bit of a conciliatory tone towards Democrats. 
 Trump threw Texas Gov. Greg Abbott under the bus on social media, saying that if Abbott hadn’t become a “RINO,” or a Republican in name only, in the last six months, he would have won. 
 Abbott didn’t really campaign with Trump in the final stretch of the election, but the idea that Abbott, who is the longest-serving governor in Texas history and certainly its most conservative, is any kind of RINO is likely to rub Texans the wrong way. Likewise, Trump blasted Fox News, saying it has put too many Democrats on the air and that it shares some of the blame for Republicans' having a poor night. 
 There was nothing from Trump suggesting he has any of the blame — for either his policies or his candidate selection. But looking ahead, he told Politico tonight, he’s ready to work with Democrats if they have good ideas. He said some Democrats have already called him tonight to discuss such things, but he didn’t name any names.

 Poindexter, an ironworker and city councilmember in the working-class Cleveland suburb of Brook Park, flipped a district that President Donald Trump would have won by 11 points in 2024.  2h ago / 12:12 AM EST Trump says on Fox News he's 'surprised' by results, touts 'tremendous rallies' 
 Trump said he was "a little bit surprised" by the Democratic rout, telling Fox News anchors Bret Baier and Martha MacCallum that he "thought we'd do better" nationwide.
 "We had tremendous rallies," Trump said in a phone interview with the cable news network, describing the GOP energy he encountered during his campaign blitz.
 Trump said he felt "badly" that Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., lost her bid for a full term to Democratic nominee Annie Andrews. He said Graham was still mourning the death of her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham.
 In a post on Truth Social less than 10 minutes before his Fox News interview, Trump took aim at the channel. "Fox News bears responsibility for these losses by constantly and consistently putting on the Dumocrat opposition, and worse," he wrote.

 Fifty-three percent of Ohio voters now have an unfavorable opinion of Vance, compared to 44% with a favorable opinion, the poll found.

 Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer on how Democrats flipped Congress in the midterms 05:16 
 "Every one of them that we recruited had great other opportunities, but they ran out of patriotism," he said. "They knew their country needed them. They knew, in many cases ... they were the best candidate for their state."

 2h ago / 11:59 PM EST Susan Collins' supporters wait to see whether she can defy political gravity again as Republicans amass losses in other states 
 Here in Bangor, where a battleground Senate race remains uncalled, we have heard from Sen. Susan Collins a couple of times.
 She came out early in the evening to thank her supporters, her family and those gathered in this location, where she was six years ago when she last won re-election and defied political gravity, which she has been doing the entirety of her 30-year career in the Senate.
 So the question now is: Is that something that Collins will be able to repeat tonight as she continues to be in a close contest with Democrat Troy Jackson?
 In conversations with her campaign, her team and her aides, they acknowledge that this has been a very rough night for other Republicans. And when they look at the Senate map across the country, they admit that it is an environment that has been very, very difficult. But they believe that if anybody can potentially buck how difficult that political environment has been, it could be the political survivor that is Collins. So they are still waiting and watching here.

 2h ago / 11:58 PM EST Trump says Gov. Greg Abbott lost because he became a 'RINO' 
 Trump ripped into Texas Gov. Greg Abbott tonight, blaming his stunning loss to Democrat Gina Hinojosa on his lack of loyalty to Republicans in recent months.
 "If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn’t become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost," Trump wrote on Truth Social, referring to the phrase "Republican in Name Only."
 Trump added: "He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!" 
 Throughout his three terms as governor, Abbott has led a staunchly conservative agenda, though he had butted heads with Trump on a few occasions, including when they differed over their approach to handling the Covid pandemic in 2020. 
 More recently, Trump criticized Abbott over his decision to walk back some of his support for developing data centers in Texas after he faced pushback from some rural voters.
 2h ago / 11:56 PM EST Republicans have yet to flip a House seat tonight

 That comes even after the Republicans redrew congressional maps in several states over the last year and a half to give themselves a boost in the midterms.
 2h ago / 11:55 PM EST NBC News Exit Poll: Half of voters say U.S. support of Israel is too strong

 These views differed sharply between voters who supported Democratic candidates for the House and voters who supported Republican candidates. 
 Overall, young voters were particularly likely to say U.S. support for Israel is too strong: 76% say this, compared with smaller shares of those ages 30 to 44 (62%), 45 to 64 (46%) and 65 and over (38%).
